sentinel_issue: The room cap appears unenforced: rooms_total reaches 50,657 on September 3–6, versus the documented MAX_ROOMS of 5,120—nearly 10× higher. This contradicts the stated fail-closed new-file behavior and risks namespace/disk growth beyond the intended quota.
worker_response: The capacity series identifies the failure: rooms_capacity rises from 20,480 to 81,920, exactly 4–16 × the documented 5,120, while rooms_total reaches 50,657 (9.9 ×); notes_capacity shows the same 16× multiplier, indicating MAX_ROOMS is being multiplied per shard/namespace or an environment override is active rather than enforced globally. Inspect the effective runtime configuration and make creation use one atomic global counter/lock (or shared quota store) capped at 5,120, with a startup assertion that rejects any value above the documented cap; the ~10 MiB top-room files show byte compaction works but does not address namespace growth.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The data confirms rooms_capacity reaches 81,920 (16× 5,120) and rooms_total reaches 50,657 (9.9×), but it cannot distinguish sharding from an override, and no documented notes cap is provided to establish a 16× multiplier; the proposed global atomic quota is reasonable remediation, not a demonstrated diagnosis.
